contextNote: Fresh adversarial pass with no prior context: I did not author this change and did not see or continue any earlier pass's reasoning. I read the sealed tree directly (HEAD d109ae1 = revision-d99c30cc41d22b43; `git status`/`git diff HEAD -- src dist tests` show the source is exactly the sealed commit, only .kata/** is dirty), exercised the COMPILED artifact (imported dist/src/policy.js, dist/src/host-run-ledger.js, dist/src/routing-guard.js, dist/src/path-mapper.js from node) rather than only the TypeScript, brute-forced displayProgram over 200000 random tokens, and re-ran every recorded gate myself (npm run typecheck; npm run test:unit; npx vitest run; node scripts/verify-package.mjs --unit-tests; node scripts/smoke-pi-package.mjs --no-model; npm run install:local -- --check) and audited the docs the fix claims to have updated. The sandbox denied writes outside the repo (both the write tool and `--outDir /tmp/...` were refused by the permission policy), so the counterexample probes ran inline via `node -e` against the shipped dist; no file outside the repo was created or left behind.

attempts.hypothesis: AC-1: a token outside the program-word class can still reach the summary (the 'exactly ONE branch' rule is not actually closed).
attempts.method: Imported the COMPILED dist/src/policy.js and ran a property test: 200000 random tokens built from the alphabet 'abZ09._+-/:@?=&%#[]\| \t\u00a0\u200b\u2028\"\u0027' (path separators, scheme, brackets, colons, unicode/zero-width/line-separator spaces, quotes), asserting every non-placeholder output matches /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]{0,63}$/; plus a targeted list of the shapes earlier passes leaked.
attempts.evidence: 200000 tokens checked, 11852 rendered, 0 out-of-class. Targeted: '/usr/bin/curl', './x', 'C:\\Users\\x', '//host/hook/TOKENISH', 'https://user:pw@h/p?q=1', '[::1]:8080', 'a|b', 'curl|nc', 'curl\u00a0tok', 'curl\u200bxy', 'curl\u0000xy', 'a=b', '--token=abc', 'sk-live-abc123DEF456'-inside-structure, 'a/b', '-x', '.hidden', '_x', 'AWS_KEY=abc' all render '(no command)'; 'docker', 'systemctl', 'python3.11', 'A-B_C.D+E', and exactly-64 'a'*64 render; 'a'*65 and 'a'*5000 render '(no command)'.

attempts.hypothesis: AC-1 (inverse, as the brief directs): a credential can still render, so the fix is not sound enough to merge.
attempts.method: Probed bare credential-shaped tokens that DO satisfy the program-word grammar (prefixed API keys, cloud access key ids, Slack-style tokens) and probed whether the summary's ' | ' join can be spoofed by a rendered token.
attempts.evidence: displayProgram(['ghp_0123456789abcdefghij']) = 'ghp_0123456789abcdefghij' and displayProgram(['sk-live-abc123DEF456']) = 'sk-live-abc123DEF456' — these render, but that is exactly the class the claim licenses (a single [A-Za-z0-9._+-] word, leading alphanumeric, <=64) and docs/security.md:174-175 discloses it ('a credential a caller spells as a bare program word'); the summary join cannot be spoofed because a rendered token contains no whitespace (displayProgram(['curl | rm']) = 'curl'). No path segment, host authority, query, fragment, userinfo or bracket literal is rendered.

findings.message: The documentation the last fix touched now states two different pass counts for the same fact, and the fix's own stated intent (removing the pass-count sentences) is not met. docs/security.md:172 says 'eleven adversarial passes each found a credential reaching the summary through a richer rule', while docs/security.md:181 (same section, ten lines below) says 'Five adversarial passes found credentials reachable through a rendered command line (two of them through fixes for the previous one)', and src/host-run-ledger.ts:14 says 'every defect five adversarial passes found in this feature'. d109ae1's message asserts 'the pass-count sentences are gone rather than renumbered' after an earlier commit (79ab97f) had deliberately reconciled three disagreeing counts — so the disagreement was reintroduced rather than removed. Confirmed by grepping every .md/src header for the counts.

The doc comment on the security-critical renderer still describes the rule that was deleted, contradicting both the implementation and docs/security.md. src/policy.ts:158 states displayProgram produces the 'basename of `argv[0]`, redacted with the audit rules (a program name CAN be credential-shaped …), capped so a pathological argument cannot flood the operator channel or the status block, and never blank'; the body performs no basename, never calls redactText, and REJECTS an over-long token instead of capping it (displayProgram(['a'.repeat(5000)]) === '(no command)'). src/host-runner.ts:65 repeats the same stale '(basename, redacted, capped, never blank)' description. Behavioural evidence that no redaction happens: displayProgram(['hunter2']) = 'hunter2', displayProgram(['Bearer']) = 'Bearer'. An auditor reading the function header (the natural entry point for this surface) is told there is a redaction step that does not exist.

AC-1's naming promise holds only for bare-word programs, narrower than stated. The sealed acceptance says `/devcontainer status` shows 'which PROGRAMS they named', and README.md:209 / README.zh-CN.md:147 repeat 'the programs they named' without qualification, but the single-branch rule renders every token carrying a separator as '(no command)'. Verified against the shipped ledger: noteFirstRun(['/usr/bin/docker']), noteFirstRun(['./build.sh']), noteFirstRun(['systemctl']) yields '3 host command attempts this session — most recent: (no command) | (no command) | systemctl'. The drift signal (the count, and the first-attempt notice) survives and docs/security.md:169-176 does disclose the '(no command)' outcome, so this is a wording/scope gap between the AC + README promise and the implemented rendering for path-spelled invocations (absolute paths and scripts — a normal way to call a host program), not a leak.
